Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings: 41-year-old man with 2-month history of fatigue, insomnia, decreased appetite, low mood, anhedonia, decreased libido, exertional SOB, background hypothyroidism on thyroxine. No current suicidality.

Working impressions:  
• Major depressive disorder or adjustment disorder – symptoms meet multiple DSM-5 criteria; onset linked to occupational stressor.  
• Possible sub-optimally treated hypothyroidism – similar symptom cluster; needs TFTs to assess adequacy of replacement.  
• Other contributors (e.g., anemia, nutritional deficiency) less likely but need exclusion.

Plan: Arrange in-person GP review for full physical examination and targeted investigations (thyroid function tests, CBC, iron studies, B-12/folate, electrolytes, renal/liver profile, fasting glucose & lipids). Consider mental health screening tools (PHQ-9, GAD-7). Discuss possible psychological support and lifestyle measures. Reassess once results available.

Management Plan

- Book face-to-face GP appointment within next few days (patient agreed)  
- At visit: conduct full physical exam including vitals, BMI, cardiorespiratory and mental state assessment  
- Order blood tests: TFTs, CBC, iron studies, B-12/folate, U&E, LFT, fasting glucose & lipids ± vitamin D  
- Review thyroxine adherence and dosing; adjust if required based on TFTs  
- Provide information on sleep hygiene, balanced diet, regular gentle exercise as tolerated  
- Offer mental health support: discuss counselling/psychology referral after initial assessment  
- Safety net: patient to seek help if mood deteriorates or suicidal thoughts emerge  
- Schedule follow-up once investigations complete to review results and symptoms  

Consider:

- Allied health referral (EPC – 10 visits): Not recorded  
- Reproductive or sexual health clinic referral: Not recorded  
- Mental health support if indicated (e.g., psychologist, AMS support): Discussed; to be considered after assessment  
- CTG registration: Not recorded  
- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test): Not recorded  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):

1. Major depressive disorder / adjustment disorder – High likelihood: symptom constellation (low mood, anhedonia, fatigue, insomnia, appetite ↓, concentration ↓, libido ↓) and temporal relationship to job change.  
2. Sub-optimally treated hypothyroidism – Moderate likelihood: known history plus overlapping symptoms; requires TFTs to confirm.  
3. Anemia (iron-deficiency or other) – Low-moderate likelihood: fatigue and exertional SOB with reduced dietary intake; needs CBC/iron studies.

● No contradictions identified between transcript and DDx (single confusion over morning erections, clarified).  
● Transcript quality: clear audio; minor freezing but did not affect clinical content.
